limitations: Research / decision-support prototype; not certified for navigation or safety-critical operational use.
The sea-ice forecast does not beat persistence in a statistically trusted way: trust horizon 0 days against persistence (21 days against damped persistence and climatology).
Iceberg drift is only slightly better than assuming no movement on position; its demonstrated value is probabilistic (coverage near nominal), confirmed on 5-6 tracks in 2024-25.
The vessel is a generic polar research vessel and its ice class is a placeholder (REPLACE_WITH_VERIFIED_CLASS); fuel is an index, not tonnes.
The isotonic forecast-probability calibrator is validated for per-cell P(C >= 0.15) but is NOT applied to route risk; route risk counts breaches over joint scenarios with a Wilson bound.
This end-to-end result is not evidence that calibrated probabilities are used, and the 1.88 % Wilson bound is the floor for 0 breaches in 200 scenarios, not evidence of forecast skill.
One demonstration window only; USNIC positions are weekly and currents are daily at 0.5 m depth on a 25 km grid.
